workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the product, commercial goals, target audience, supplied photography, Tmall constraints, required claims, purchase information, scope, approvals, and conversion success criteria.
Investigate audience needs, category conventions, competitor detail pages, purchase barriers, and the evidence available to support product benefits.
Establish defensible messaging, hierarchy, credibility, mobile readability, and visual-conversion principles for the page.
Define the mobile-first page architecture, module sequence, image and copy hierarchy, dimensions, calls to action, specifications, reassurance content, and asset requirements.
Develop meaningfully different visual and narrative directions using representative modules such as the opening screen, benefit section, and product-detail section.
Compare the concepts against audience, brand, clarity, differentiation, feasibility, and conversion criteria, then obtain explicit client approval of one direction.
Apply feedback to the selected direction, finalize copy-image relationships, retouching treatment, hierarchy, and representative page modules while preserving approved decisions.
Extend the approved direction across the complete Tmall detail page, including benefit, proof, usage, specification, purchase, and reassurance modules.
Validate factual accuracy, visual consistency, mobile legibility, platform compliance, export quality, and asset completeness before packaging the agreed final files.

missing_inputs: Product identity, category, features, specifications, variants, pricing, and availability
Target audience, positioning, purchase motivations, objections, and intended traffic sources
Full-resolution raw photographs, file inventory, usage rights, and information about available angles or missing shots
Brand guidelines, logos, fonts, colours, existing campaign materials, and mandatory marketplace conventions
Approved product claims, substantiation, certifications, legal disclaimers, warranty, shipping, returns, and customer-service information
Required page copy, language requirements, tone of voice, and responsibility for copywriting or translation
Tmall template, current technical specifications, target dimensions, file-size limits, and module constraints
Competitor set, desired differentiation, benchmark pages, and prohibited visual territory
Conversion objectives, baseline performance, analytics availability, testing plan, schedule, budget, and approval stakeholders
assumptions: The primary output is a mobile-first Tmall product detail page rather than a new brand identity or a new photography shoot.
The supplied raw photographs will be licensed, sufficiently high resolution, and suitable for retouching and compositing once provided.
All product benefits and purchase claims will require client-supplied evidence and approval before publication.
A representative concept will be approved before the visual system is expanded across the full page.
Chinese-language copy, platform compliance, and final commercial terms will be supplied or approved by qualified stakeholders.
stop_conditions: Do not begin visual development until the product, audience, commercial objective, usable source photographs, and core page requirements are available.
Do not select or expand a direction without explicit human or client approval of a representative concept.
Do not publish unsupported product claims, certifications, comparisons, prices, promotions, shipping terms, warranties, or other purchase information.
Do not complete production exports until Tmall technical requirements, final approved copy, legal content, product specifications, and image usage rights are confirmed.
Stop and request new photography or a revised scope if the supplied images cannot support the approved structure, required product views, or acceptable output quality.
rationale: The workflow first establishes commercial and evidentiary foundations, then converts them into design principles and a mobile-first content structure. Distinct concepts are evaluated before refinement and full-page expansion, limiting rework while ensuring the final Tmall page communicates benefits, proof, specifications, and purchase information clearly.
